oewn-07537871-n.learner: a worried feeling about what is going to happen.
examples: As for Jane, her anxiety under this suspense was, of course, more painful than Elizabeth's
She could not bear such suspense

oewn-07526477-n.learner: an excited feeling as you wait for the most important moment of something to come.
examples: The last scene of the film kept the whole audience in suspense.

oewn-05707735-n.learner: a state of not knowing or not being sure about something.
examples: The question of who owned the land stayed in suspense for years.

oewn-00225476-r.learner: in a violent way, with rough and sudden force.
examples: The two men fought violently in the street.

oewn-02133338-v.learner: to see or notice something, or to be alive at the time when something happens.
examples: I could then perceive that his partiality for Miss Bennet was beyond what I had ever witnessed in him.
The last century witnessed huge changes in the way people travel.

oewn-02132751-v.learner: to be a witness to something, that is, to be there and see it happen.
examples: She witnessed the accident and later told the police what she saw.

oewn-00386914-r.learner: in a keen or piercing way, so that something is felt or noticed very sharply.
examples: Darcy seemed to feel it most acutely
how acutely did she now feel it!

oewn-00141793-r.learner: in a way that starts suddenly and quickly.
examples: The child became acutely ill during the night.

oewn-00274018-r.learner: in a clever way that quickly sees what is really going on.
examples: He was acutely insightful about what his rivals wanted.

oewn-00505194-r.learner: in a way that changes direction suddenly and by a large amount.
examples: Her shoes had acutely pointed toes.

oewn-00073656-a.learner: speaking or behaving in a way that is not natural, in order to impress people.
examples: her voice was weak, and her manner affected.

connotation.why: calls the behaviour put-on and false, not just unusual

oewn-01564296-a.learner: stirred up so that you show a strong feeling.
examples: Though Lydia had never been a favourite with them, Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner could not but be deeply affected.

oewn-14019309-n.learner: the freedom to decide what to do, or to judge something, for yourself.
examples: How much to tip is left to your discretion.

oewn-04898205-n.learner: the quality of judging things wisely and fairly, without being swayed by your own feelings.
examples: A judge must show discretion when weighing both sides of a case.

oewn-05759704-n.learner: fine, careful good taste, and a sense of how to act or speak without upsetting people.
examples: The room was decorated with discretion and quiet taste.

oewn-05206024-n.learner: the power to make your own choices without being controlled by anything outside you.
examples: The preacher said that every person has the discretion to choose between good and evil.

oewn-07155367-n.learner: a talk in which people share their ideas and opinions about a subject.
examples: The discussion of Mr. Collins's offer was now nearly at an end
the Brighton scheme, of which Lydia had given them a hint at the inn, was under frequent discussion between her parents.

oewn-07152793-n.learner: a long piece of speech or writing about one subject, often with people answering each other.
examples: The book contains a clear discussion of how plants grow.

oewn-02070438-v.learner: to move or go on freely and smoothly, like water in a stream.
examples: as his composure convinced her that all was safe, her wit flowed along.
My ideas flow so rapidly that I have not time to express them
The river flows past the old mill.

oewn-01545450-v.learner: to hang or fall down loosely in a particular way.
examples: Her long hair flowed down over her shoulders.

oewn-02749602-v.learner: to be there in large amounts.
examples: At the wedding the wine flowed all night.
The engineers flowed cool air over the engine to test it.

oewn-00217853-v.learner: to cover or flood something with water.
examples: The farmers flowed water over the rice fields.

oewn-00061974-v.learner: to have a period, the monthly bleeding from the womb.
examples: She was flowing heavily that week and felt tired.
His hearing got worse as he grew older.

oewn-01202187-n.learner: in law, a meeting, usually held by a court, where evidence is taken so that the facts can be settled and a decision made from that evidence.
examples: The court will hold a hearing next week to decide who owns the house.

oewn-14508362-n.learner: a chance to explain your side of things and be listened to.
examples: Everyone deserves a fair hearing before being punished.

oewn-08578322-n.learner: the distance within which a voice can be heard.
examples: She waited until he was out of hearing before she spoke.

oewn-00883837-n.learner: the act of listening carefully to something.
examples: Give their new songs a hearing before you judge them.

oewn-07161975-n.learner: a meeting of a committee or a grand jury where witnesses are called and asked to give evidence.
examples: The committee held a public hearing on the new law.

oewn-03546876-n.learner: a hotel where travellers can stay the night.
examples: After welcoming their sisters, they triumphantly displayed a table set out with such cold meat as an inn larder usually affords
